agree.reason: The cost breakdown and the candour about being a first-time creator will reassure this backer somewhat, but with no delivery date, refund promise or update schedule, someone who has already lost $85 is unlikely to pledge on this page alone.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the 'proven hit' claim and admits only 23 people have rated the game, but 'every one of them' played a whole winter and then chose to rate it goes beyond the brief and hides that most raters played at the designer's own table, and 'changed every rule' and 'every session tells a different winter' are claims the brief doesn't support.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out correctly that the goal needs 572 backers, that making and shipping their copies costs $22,548 and that about $5,450 is left over, but it never puts the roughly $2,800 in fees against that remainder to show the real cushion, and it doesn't give the unit cost of $11.60.

right_comparison.reason: The only alternative it describes is that the game isn't made and nobody is charged if the goal is missed; it never sets the risk of this project against the reader's real choice of backing a first-time creator's campaign.

qualification.reason: The all-or-nothing condition at $28,000 has a number and a consequence the reader can check, but the page gives no delivery date, no refund trigger if delivery runs late and no update schedule, and the hedge on the small number of ratings carries no consequence.

objections.reason: It raises the first-time-creator worry and answers it with a slogan about being a careful land surveyor instead of the concrete safeguards a wary backer needs (finished art and rules, a signed factory quote, a refund promise, regular updates).

fit.reason: It is a well-structured crowdfunding pitch of about 500 words, as the brief asked.
